## Data containers are in core

```{r}
#| label: data_container

# Load libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(ggforce)

# Adjusting the text positions for better alignment
ellipse_data <- data.frame(
    x = c(0, 0, 0),         # Centers of ellipses
    y = c(2, 1, 0),         # Centers of ellipses
    a = c(4, 3, 2),         # Widths of ellipses
    b = c(3, 2, 1),         # Heights of ellipses
    label = c("COMMUNITY", "METHODS", "DATA CONTAINER"),  # Labels for each ellipse
    label_y = c(4, 1.75, 0) # Adjusted vertical positions for labels
)

# Plot with adjusted labels
ggplot() +
    geom_ellipse(data = ellipse_data, 
                 aes(x0 = x, y0 = y, a = a, b = b, angle = 0),
                 color = "darkgreen", fill = "grey90", alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_text(data = ellipse_data, 
              aes(x = x, y = label_y, label = label), 
              size = 5, fontface = "bold") +
    coord_fixed() +
    theme_void()
```

::: {.notes}
In Bioconductor, the core of software is formed by data containers.

When we agree with the data format, developers can develop interoperable methods and packages that then the users can utilize to analyze their data.
:::

## `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("SummarizedExperiment")`
<small>[@Huber2015]</small>

![](images/SE.png){fig-alt="SummarizedExperiment class" fig-align="center" width=10%}

::: {.notes}
SummarizedExperiment was develop for generic data container for biological data analysis.

Nowadays, it is the main data container adpoted by many fields.

Genomics, metabolomics, ...
:::

## `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("TreeSummarizedExperiment")`
<small>[@Huang2021]</small>

![](images/TreeSE.png){fig-alt="TreeSummarizedExperiment class" fig-align="center" width=10%}

::: {.notes}
Microbiome field was using different data container. It is like dancing the disco dance alone while others are dancing in the dance floor.
If you are Zulip (you should), you can find a video of disco dance instructions.

So Huang and others extended this SummarizedExperimet class to support trees which is a typical format to present bacterial phylogeny trees.
:::


## Orchestrating Microbiome Analysis, OMA

```{r}
#| label: mia_stats
#| eval: true

library(BiocPkgTools)

perc <- pkgDownloadRank("mia")
perc <- paste0(perc, "%")

df <-biocDownloadStats()
df <- df[df$Package == "mia", ]

years <- firstInBioc(df)[["Year"]]:as.integer(format(Sys.Date(), "%Y"))

base_url <- "https://bioconductor.org/packages/stats/bioc/mia"
all_data <- list()

for (yr in years) {
    url <- sprintf("%s/mia_%d_stats.tab", base_url, yr)
    # try downloading safely
    try({
        df <- read.delim(url)
        df$Year <- yr
        all_data[[as.character(yr)]] <- df
    }, silent=TRUE)
}

all_data <- do.call(rbind, all_data)
df <- all_data[all_data[["Month"]] == "all", ]

last_year <- sort(df[["Year"]])[ which(sort(df[["Year"]]) == as.integer(format(Sys.Date(), "%Y")))-1 ]

num_downloads <- df[df[["Year"]] == last_year, "Nb_of_distinct_IPs"]
num_downloads <- floor(num_downloads / 1000) * 1000

num_downloads <- paste0(format(num_downloads, big.mark = ","))
```

- Microbiome data science ecosystem
- Packages (`r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("mia")` top `r if(exists("perc")) perc else "*ERROR*"` in Bioconductor)
- Bioconductor book

## Building the microbiome community in Bioconductor

- Common data standard `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("TreeSummarizedExperiment")`
- Interoperable software (methods from international community)
- Shared knowledge (online book)
- Open collaboration

::: notes
We now have the infrastructure, methods, and documentation.

The next challenge is not technical.

The challenge is building a community where developers, researchers, and users work together on common standards and interoperable tools.

Something that I look up is the tidyomics community. They have been very successful building their community, and I want that microbiome will have something similar in the future. 

:::
